FindName: Suez Inscriptions of Darius the Great
Description: Five monuments set up along Darius the Great's canal through Wadi Tumilat, joining the Nile to the Red Sea, inscribed in Old Persian, Elamite, Babylonian, and Egyptian. The best preserved, the pink granite Chalouf (Shaluf) Stele found in 1866, records in Darius's own voice: 'I am a Persian; setting out from Persia I conquered Egypt. I ordered to dig this canal from the river that is called Nile... to the sea that begins in Persia.'
Interpretations: Scholars agree the stelae commemorate Darius's canal; classical authors disagree on whether Darius actually completed the canal or whether it was finished under Ptolemy II, and Darius's claim to have 'conquered Egypt' overstates the record, since Cambyses II had conquered Egypt before him.
AlternativeNames: Chalouf Stele; Shaluf Stele; Darius Canal Stelae
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Rebuilding of the Temple
RelatedPeople: Darius the Persian; Cyrus the Great; Zerubbabel; Ezra; Nehemiah
BiblicalSignificance: Darius is the Persian king of the world in which the exiles returned and the temple was rebuilt, and these stelae are his own voice claiming Egypt and the canal as his achievement. They set the stage for Ezra and Nehemiah: a Persian empire that could move armies, officials, and temple vessels across continents, and whose kings' decrees shaped Judah's restoration.
CurrentLocation: Louvre, Paris (Chalouf Stele fragment); other monuments fragmentary or lost
